scope: Planning refinements only. No generated textures, painting, approved-art changes or runtime species definitions. Research covers the named analogues, not every alias in the full roster.
shared_implementation: Generate neutral reusable swatches after the raw queue. Coat configurations are anatomical masks and colour transforms over shared fur, not separate generated models or extra runtime materials. Bake one atlas per selected coat; switch atlases without extra draw calls. Eye/socket geometry and gloss remain separate from fur. All numerical morph bounds are proposed art limits, not measured biological distributions.

real_analogues: White-tailed summer/winter and fawn patterns
Chital-like persistent spotting; morphology still needs review
Deer.texture_assets: Reuse accepted directional fur. Five shared surface classes: fur, glossy eye, nose/lid skin, hoof keratin and inner-ear skin. Two authored spot masks (adult and juvenile), one optional stripe mask; pale throat/belly/tail and face masks shared across coats. No new swatch per hue.
Deer.sex_age_season: Keep the approved 50/50 antlered/antlerless review roll. A future lineage rule must also account for age and seasonal antler loss: antlerless does not always mean female. Adult-male neck fullness is a bounded later morph; fawns need juvenile proportions rather than an adult shrunk uniformly. Summer/winter colour transition preserves permanent pale regions.
Deer.extras: Retain approved four rack shapes, eye/lid/whisker work and ear/tail traits. Later add velvet/bare-antler material states and a no-rack seasonal state without changing the body rig. Reindeer remains its separate roster entry; do not copy this male-only antler rule to it.
Deer.paint_details: Smooth continuous throat/belly blend; feather pale muzzle into fur, not a hard neck band. White-tail underside is a tail-local mask. Fit iris, bare lid rim and front canthus to actual landmarks, not a circular dark stamp.
Deer.hypotheses: Optional weak adult flank bands in patchy thicket light and paler sandy coats in dry open habitat. These are design hypotheses, not claimed wild species or automatically superior camouflage.
Deer.geometry_limits: A chital-like mask is not proof of chital anatomy. Muntjac, heavy-necked sambar and distinct red-deer silhouettes require separate proportion/head approval; do not force every roster alias onto one doe mesh.

real_analogues: European brown hare
Snowshoe hare summer/winter
coat_configurations: white snowshoe winter with dark ear tips
Hare.texture_assets: Five reusable surface classes: directional coat fur, denser foot fur, eye, bare nose/lid skin and inner-ear skin. Share the coat swatch with palette shifts; separate ear-tip, belly, tail-top/underside and seasonal-whitening masks. No pink bare paw pads painted onto densely furred snowshoe soles.
Hare.sex_age_season: No obligatory sex-specific coat. Do not apply a universal larger-male rule: snowshoe females can be larger. The European analogue stays brown/grey in winter; whitening belongs only to an appropriate snow-adapted lineage. Juvenile proportions and ear/foot growth need separate later approval.
Hare.extras: After selection: whiskers, glossy lateral eyes with proper lids, bounded ear length/width and foot-fur thickness. Use linked ear/foot/body traits rather than independent extreme sliders that produce a rabbit silhouette.
Hare.paint_details: Keep black ear tips through snowshoe winter whitening. European tail top dark/underside pale; broad soft belly blend and warm face/limbs. Whitening follows fur regions and never bleaches the eye, nose or exposed lid.
Hare.hypotheses: A pale sandy lineage in dry grassland and a darker peatland lineage are optional pigment designs. Strong adult stripes or decorative spots are not a default hare requirement.
Hare.geometry_limits: Long-legged long-eared European and broad-footed snowshoe forms may exceed a small local morph. Arctic and mountain-hare aliases remain explicit shape/reference checks; they are not yet researched as exact copies.

real_analogues: Wild European rabbit
Rabbit.texture_assets: Five surface classes as for the hare, with shorter coat/foot fur. Reuse neutral fur and shared eye/nose/ear assets. One agouti modulation mask and separate pale belly/tail underside masks; optional low-contrast mottling is a mask, not another model.
Rabbit.sex_age_season: Keep the same coat pool for both sexes; avoid a large ornamental dewlap or domestic-breed dimorphism by default. Wild European rabbits do not receive the hare's automatic white winter coat. Dependent naked newborns are outside this adult prototype; later juveniles need compact age proportions.
Rabbit.extras: Shorter ears and less elongated hindlimbs than the hare, small tail, fitted eyes/lids and whiskers. No lop ears, extreme dwarf heads or giant domestic breeds in the default wild lineage.
Rabbit.paint_details: Agouti variation stays fine enough to read as fur, with pale grey belly and white underside of the tail. Soft eye surround and warm ear interior must follow the inner bowl; outer rim remains furred.
Rabbit.hypotheses: Sandy pale and faint litter-mottled wild lineages are optional ecology-linked art. A snow-white seasonal lineage would be invented here, not a normal European-rabbit seasonal state.
Rabbit.geometry_limits: Do not substitute the hare body or call domestic-breed extremes natural wild-rabbit variation. The approved mesh must keep its compact rabbit silhouette.

real_analogues: Red, cross, silver and black phases of Vulpes vulpes
coat_configurations: red with dark legs and pale underside
Red fox.texture_assets: Six surface classes: short face/leg fur, longer body/tail fur, eye, nose/lid skin, paw pad and claw keratin. Share two fur swatches across coats. Separate cross-saddle, silver guard-tip and dark stocking masks; white tail-tip/chin/underside masks are retained across these analogue phases.
Red fox.sex_age_season: Coat phase is independent of sex and can vary within a lineage. Use modest overlapping size ranges rather than male-only dark coats. Winter density is a linked coat-length/normal treatment, not a white recolour. Young keep age-specific face/ear proportions later.
Red fox.extras: Fitted lids, muzzle whiskers, furred ear rim and a full tail silhouette after motion approval. Bound ear/tail changes together; keep the straight non-curled tail.
Red fox.paint_details: Dark outer ears and lower legs, pale inner ear/chin/ventral regions, soft flank blending. Silver phase uses scattered pale guard tips over dark fur instead of flat grey. Inspect white tail-tip placement from rear and during turns.
Red fox.hypotheses: A paler dryland red coat is a bounded palette design. Do not label a silver red fox as an arctic fox or assume rare morphs should occupy equal proportions in a natural population.
Red fox.geometry_limits: Arctic, fennec and grey foxes need independent anatomical consideration; this red-fox mesh is not made equivalent by changing colour or tail tip.

real_analogues: Grey-wolf colour range: white, grizzled grey, brown and black
Wolf.texture_assets: Six shared classes: short facial fur, coarse body/ruff fur, eye, nose/lid skin, paw-pad skin and claw keratin. One saddle/face/underside mask set with palette and guard-tip controls; no unique body texture generation for each grey value.
Wolf.sex_age_season: Sex does not select a separate colour family. Plan overlapping body-size ranges and modest neck fullness only after skin checks. Winter thickness is a bounded fur/roughness change; northern pale appearance is lineage-linked, not all wolves turning white each winter. Juveniles need age proportions, not only scale.
Wolf.extras: Muzzle whiskers, eye/lid transitions and a restrained ruff/tail silhouette after approval. Keep a long-legged wolf profile, small-to-moderate upright ears and a non-curled tail.
Wolf.paint_details: Blend the dark back into flank grizzle and pale chin/belly; preserve fur direction at shoulder and neck. Black coats still need roughness/guard-hair contrast, while ivory coats keep dark nose/lid and non-emissive shadow response.
Wolf.hypotheses: Bounded sandy or darker wet-cover pigment designs may be tested; habitat alone must not force every individual into the same coat. No invented coat is presented as a verified taxon.
Wolf.geometry_limits: Do not create domestic-dog breeds through random skull/leg extremes. A compact arctic-like coat can share the core only if its body and motion remain acceptable.

real_analogues: Eurasian wild-boar brown/black/grey adults and striped piglets
Wild boar.texture_assets: Six classes: bristle/body hair, snout/lid skin, eye, hoof keratin, tusk ivory and temporary mud. One adult grizzle mask, one longitudinal piglet-stripe mask, rough snout and limb/underside regions. Mud is a removable state overlay, not a genetic coat.
Wild boar.sex_age_season: Larger mature-male head/shoulders and tusks are linked age/sex traits, with smaller female tusks where visible; no antler-style 50/50 tusk rule. Stripes fade with juvenile growth rather than appearing on ordinary adults. Seasonal coat density and wallowing dirt are separate from lineage colour.
Wild boar.extras: Two or three tusk-size shapes plus a no-visible-tusk juvenile state, coarse dorsal bristles, short straight tufted tail, snout disc and properly seated eyes. Add only after selecting motion-compatible head/body geometry.
Wild boar.paint_details: Bristles are coarse directional fibres with lighter tips. Nose disc/nostrils and hoof edges need anatomical masks; juvenile stripes run along flanks rather than around the body. Avoid domestic pink patchwork as the default wild-boar appearance.
Wild boar.hypotheses: Optional warmer open-habitat brown and weakly retained juvenile striping are hypothetical lineage designs; neither is required for the baseline.
Wild boar.geometry_limits: Do not turn wild boar into warthog, peccary or a domestic short-faced pig by recolouring. Those have separate roster anatomy.

real_analogues: European mouflon-type short coat, adult ram saddle and variable female horns
coat_configurations: rufous brown adult ram with pale saddle
dark winter ram with stronger saddle
Mouflon.texture_assets: Five classes: short coarse coat, eye, nose/lid skin, horn/hoof keratin and inner-ear skin. One shared fur swatch; saddle, dorsal stripe, pale muzzle/eye surround, belly and lower-leg masks. Horn growth-ring normal/colour can share the goat keratin source.
Mouflon.sex_age_season: Ram horn curl and body robustness increase with maturity. Ewes use absent or small horns depending on lineage, not large ram horns at half probability. Lamb coat is closer to plain ewe colour. Seasonal saddle contrast is a coat state, not a wholly new texture source.
Mouflon.extras: Three ram horn sizes on one backward-curving spiral family, small female-horn and hornless options, short neck fringe. Do not use antler branching or domestic full-body wool.
Mouflon.paint_details: Place the pale saddle on the flanks with a deliberate but fur-soft boundary; keep pale muzzle, eye surround, belly and lower legs distinct. Retain coat direction through the neck rather than a sharp material seam.
Mouflon.hypotheses: Paler dryland brown and reduced saddle contrast are optional plausible designs. Expanded white patches are hypotheses, not a claim of another established mouflon species.
Mouflon.geometry_limits: Horns are keratin appendages with age/sex controls; the short-coated mouflon body is not a ready wool sheep, bighorn or argali without new silhouette approval. Taxonomic naming varies by source; use visual analogue rather than claiming a resolved taxonomy.

real_analogues: Bezoar-type wild goat with backward horns in both sexes
Wild goat.texture_assets: Five classes: coarse coat, eye, nose/lid skin, horn/hoof keratin and ear skin. Share the sheep/goat coat swatch with palette and hair-scale adjustments. Dorsal/shoulder/leg dark masks and pale belly are independent of horn material.
Wild goat.sex_age_season: Both sexes can have horns; mature males get thicker longer horn geometry and a stronger head/neck silhouette, females shorter thinner horns. Young use short horn buds. Winter coat and male marking intensity are linked age/season configurations, not arbitrary sex-colour swaps.
Wild goat.extras: Two or three backward-curving scimitar horn profiles plus age scales, short beard variants and modest neck fringe. Keep appendage roots fixed to the selected skull and bind beard details to head/neck.
Wild goat.paint_details: Dark dorsal line continues through the back without an atlas seam; shoulder/leg markings follow anatomy. Bare nose and eyelids get a distinct roughness region. Preserve furred outer ears with a softer inner-ear transition.
Wild goat.hypotheses: A paler arid lineage or less contrasted dark marks can be proposed. A spiral markhor rack is a different lineage/shape decision, not a random horn mutation added to every wild goat.
Wild goat.geometry_limits: Keep mountain-goat anatomy and the separate ibex entry distinct; mountain goat itself is not a queued roster entry. Extreme horn/neck/coat changes require another approved shape rather than uncontrolled morphing of the same skeleton.

real_analogues: American black bear
Brown/grizzly bear
Bear.texture_assets: Six classes: coarse body fur, shorter facial fur, eye, nose/lid skin, paw-pad skin and claw keratin. Share neutral fur across palette variants; use separate grizzled-tip and optional chest-patch masks. Skin undercoat must remain continuous at shoulder/neck.
Bear.sex_age_season: Use overlapping size distributions with larger mature males as a later body/proportion variant; colour alone never defines sex. Seasonal fat and coat fullness are bounded silhouette changes requiring motion recheck. Cubs need a rounder head/shorter muzzle and age proportions, not only a smaller adult.
Bear.extras: Two body archetypes are justified if both aliases are implemented: brown-bear shoulder hump/dished profile/longer claws, black-bear flatter shoulder/straighter profile/more prominent ears. Add fitted eyes/lids and nose detail after each archetype's motion passes.
Bear.paint_details: Keep black coats visibly furred through subtle roughness and guard-tip contrast; grizzle uses tip colouring instead of uniform grey. Pale muzzle/chest regions are anatomical masks, not a guaranteed species identifier.
Bear.hypotheses: Bounded subdued pigment or small chest-patch variation may be tried. Do not make colour an automatic proxy for aggressiveness, habitat or species; a brown coat can still belong to a black bear.
Bear.geometry_limits: One body recoloured cannot faithfully represent both black and brown bears. Preserve the current four raw auditions for selection, and mark the unrepresented archetype as needing a further shape if necessary; do not claim its geometry exists already.

real_analogues: American bison adult sexes and reddish calf
Bison.texture_assets: Six classes: long head/shoulder coat, short flank/hindquarter coat, eye, nose/lid skin, horn/hoof keratin and inner-ear skin. Two reusable fur scales with a smooth placement mask; calf colour is a palette/mask state. Spring shedding patches are a separate seasonal overlay.
Bison.sex_age_season: Both adult sexes have horns. Bulls need a broader heavier head/forequarters and larger horn profiles, cows a lighter silhouette; this is not horn/no-horn sex selection. Calves are reddish and need juvenile head/body proportions. Seasonal shedding is patchy old fur, separate from inherited coat colour.
Bison.extras: Two mature horn proportions plus young horn buds, beard and shoulder-fur silhouette treatment after motion approval. Keep the selected body's massive forequarters; avoid large extra fur-card overdraw in the prototype.
Bison.paint_details: Longer coarse fibres on head/shoulders transition to shorter flank hair without a hard neck line. Muzzle, eye rims and horn roots stay clearly placed; calf colour must not become a random adult sex coat.
Bison.hypotheses: A slightly paler or darker regional coat is an optional design. Brilliant white is not a routine camouflage preset and should be a separately considered rare pigment trait if wanted.
Bison.geometry_limits: A yak, musk ox or buffalo is not this model with a different palette. Large bull/cow or calf proportion changes require skin/motion rechecks; keep one prototype adult until selected.

real_analogues: Scale-covered butterfly/moth wings
Morpho-like blue upper wing and cryptic eyespot underside as a visual analogue
coat_configurations: blue upper wing / brown eyespot underside
Butterflies and moths (guild).texture_assets: Four classes: wing-scale detail, short body fuzz/chitin, eye gloss and antenna/leg chitin. Prepare three reusable scale/body swatches and shared eye detail; seven wing-pattern mask pairs (upper/underside), not seven model generations. Hue and pattern placement are separate controls.
Butterflies and moths (guild).sex_age_season: Select explicit lineage-specific sex pattern pairs only where wanted; no universal brighter-male rule. Adult-only prototype: caterpillar and pupa require different meshes. Seasonal wear is a later desaturation/edge-damage state, distinct from inherited markings.
Butterflies and moths (guild).extras: Use the four existing own wing-outline auditions as shape choices, not interchangeable exact species. Later add bounded antenna clubs versus moth pectination, hindwing tails only on a suitable outline, and modest body-fuzz silhouette. Keep four wing hinges and shared body rig.
Butterflies and moths (guild).paint_details: Separate dorsal and ventral wing paint, align veins continuously across each panel, and keep the body-to-wing root unpainted as fur. Blue structural colour is a controlled angle/specular response if affordable, never emissive light. Moths should not all inherit butterfly eyespots.
Butterflies and moths (guild).hypotheses: Optional low-contrast litter bands, shifted eyespot placement and greener leaf-associated palettes. Constrain changes to a coherent lineage pattern; not every random colour is a viable biological species.
Butterflies and moths (guild).geometry_limits: A swallowtail, rounded butterfly and narrow-wing moth need compatible wing outlines; female flightless moths and larval forms cannot share the default flying silhouette unchanged. No claim that these proxies are anatomically complete named species.

real_analogues: Flashing flying adult fireflies
Glow-worm/flightless-female forms are a separate representation limit
Fireflies (derived lineage).texture_assets: Four classes: beetle chitin, translucent hindwing, eye gloss and lantern/emission mask. No fur or large texture atlas required. Share a256-512 atlas per selected body; palette variants reuse chitin. Lantern colour, brightness and flash timing are parameters, not separate texture generations.
Fireflies (derived lineage).sex_age_season: The first flying proxy represents a winged adult form only. Some females are flightless and larviform; later show those as small stationary/ground glows or another approved body, not the same flying adult with wings hidden. Flash/reply timing must be linked to lineage/sex and activity conditions; not every adult firefly flashes.
Fireflies (derived lineage).extras: Optional minimal elytra silhouette after approval. No point light per insect: use a small emissive lantern or distant luminous dot, with bounded bloom. A species flash signature is more visible than extra head geometry at intended distance.
Fireflies (derived lineage).paint_details: Emission is limited to a ventral abdominal lantern, with the hard body remaining dark and non-emissive. Keep the glow from turning the entire abdomen into a uniformly illuminated plastic bulb.
Fireflies (derived lineage).hypotheses: Plausible alternate flash rhythms, response delays and modest lantern hue shifts are design hypotheses. Avoid random independent hue/rhythm for every individual of one species or universal synchronized flashing.
Fireflies (derived lineage).geometry_limits: Wingless females, larvae and daytime non-luminous adults are not all implemented by this flying model. Current review light pulse is a placeholder envelope, not a researched named-species courtship pattern.

real_analogues: Bumblebee colour/caste variants
Honeybee-like slimmer adult is a separate shape option, not a guaranteed recolour
Bees (guild).texture_assets: Four classes: body fuzz/chitin, translucent wing, compound-eye gloss and smooth leg/antenna chitin. One body-detail source with five segment-pattern masks; wing venation shared. Pollen loads are a small optional state mask/attachment, not a new species texture.
Bees (guild).sex_age_season: For a bumblebee-like lineage distinguish worker/queen female forms from males: queens larger/bulkier; male antenna/face and pollen-basket differences only if visible at gameplay scale. Male coats are species-linked, not always identical to females. Do not impose social castes on every solitary bee lineage.
Bees (guild).extras: Modest body fuzz silhouette and optional worker/queen pollen baskets after approval; no resolved stinger detail needed for an ambient speck. Four wing panels can share two coupled strokes; preserve current simple envelope animation.
Bees (guild).paint_details: Place thorax/abdomen bands by segment and preserve tail colour. Avoid painting uniform wasp stripes on every bee. Fuzz needs matte fibre detail while bare leg surfaces and eyes remain distinct.
Bees (guild).hypotheses: Additional restrained band positions or brown/ochre palettes are optional lineage designs. Keep sex/caste traits linked rather than rolling a queen abdomen onto random male markings.
Bees (guild).geometry_limits: Slender honeybee/solitary forms and round bumblebees may need different approved body choices. No full colony simulation or bee defensive AI is added by these asset plans.

real_analogues: Adult dragonfly body/wing plan
Age- and sex-linked adult colour variation
coat_configurations: brown/gold female-or-immature analogue where lineage appropriate
Dragonflies (guild).texture_assets: Four classes: body chitin/pattern, translucent veined wing, compound-eye detail and leg chitin. Shared wing-vein swatch with clear/amber/dark-patch masks; abdomen segment lines and thorax bands share one anatomical map. Colour age states reuse the same detail.
Dragonflies (guild).sex_age_season: Use lineage-specific adult male/female palettes rather than universally blue male/red female. Newly emerged adults can be pale; maturation changes belong to age state. Aquatic nymphs need a different model and are outside this flying-adult pass.
Dragonflies (guild).extras: Keep four real wing panels/hinges, slender abdomen and large eyes. Optional small wing nodus/pterostigma patches can be texture detail rather than geometry. No leg articulation or mating-clasp animation needed for the first ambient prototype.
Dragonflies (guild).paint_details: Separate wing pigmentation from transparency, preserve dark vein visibility and avoid alpha layers across large overlapping wing areas. Body gloss must remain local; coloured thorax/abdomen patterns follow segments.
Dragonflies (guild).hypotheses: Muted bog-green, amber-wing and reduced-striping lineages are optional habitat-linked designs. They are not asserted named species or proofs of evolutionary advantage.
Dragonflies (guild).geometry_limits: Damselfly eye separation, body slenderness and usually folded resting wings differ; do not call a recoloured outspread dragonfly a faithful damselfly. Broad-winged versus narrow-winged profiles need shape approval.

real_analogues: True flies with one functional wing pair
Small grey/brown and metallic detritivore visual analogues
Native detritivorous flies (guild).texture_assets: Four classes: chitin/short bristles, translucent veined wing, compound-eye detail and leg/antenna chitin. One tiny shared atlas with striped/mottled masks and hue/roughness variants. Metallic-looking cuticle is a restrained visual treatment, not a need for separate high-resolution images.
Native detritivorous flies (guild).sex_age_season: Adult-only first pass, with shared distant silhouette for both sexes. Do not invent conspicuous sex colours; any closer eye-spacing or abdomen differences need a lineage-specific later reference. Larvae are separate optional future bait/decay interactions, not shrunken flying adults.
Native detritivorous flies (guild).extras: Two functional wing panels only; the existing unused hindwing bones do not imply four visible wings. Halteres and sparse bristles can remain omitted at ambient scale. Simple hover/perch envelopes are adequate here.
Native detritivorous flies (guild).paint_details: Keep the single wing pair thin and partly transparent; compound eyes can be glossy without mammal eyelids. Thorax stripes and abdomen bands must not turn the tiny fly into a sharply striped wasp.
Native detritivorous flies (guild).hypotheses: Bounded muted pigment or metallic-hue changes can form plausible lineages. Corpse/swamp association is an ecological placement rule, not a universal visual property of every fly species.
Native detritivorous flies (guild).geometry_limits: Mosquitoes, crane flies and hoverflies are not all this compact detritivore shape. No complex flight, disease or corpse behaviour is implemented by the asset bank.

real_analogues: Mallard-like dabbling duck adult sex/season plumage
coat_configurations: brown eclipse male with residual male traits
Duck.texture_assets: Five classes: contour-feather detail, flight-feather detail, eye, bill keratin and scaled/webbed foot skin. Share two feather swatches; male/female/eclipse mask sets place head, breast, back, wing speculum and tail separately. Speculum hue and small palette shifts do not require a new model.
Duck.sex_age_season: Adult mallard-like males can become brown in eclipse; brown plumage does not universally mean female. Keep sex, maturity and molt state linked to coherent masks. Ducklings need a separate downy proportion state, not a tiny fully feathered adult.
Duck.extras: After approval: fitted lateral eyes, modest bill-shape bounds, male curled tail-feather detail only where appropriate, webbed feet. Bill and foot colour belong to the selected lineage/sex configuration.
Duck.paint_details: Feather flow follows neck/body and folded wing structure. Give upperwing speculum a deliberate bounded region, not a random blue flank spot. Separate bill from face plumage and preserve the nostril placement.
Duck.hypotheses: Optional reduced iridescence or more reed-coloured mottling are proposed lineage designs. Avoid mixing unrelated duck species head, breast and wing patches independently.
Duck.geometry_limits: Shoveler bills, pintail tails, diving-duck leg placement and domestic heavy bodies exceed a guaranteed mallard recolour. A duck swim/paddle clip is still a motion gap unless actually supplied; bird Walk/Flap alone does not implement swimming.

real_analogues: Ring-necked pheasant male/female/juvenile
coat_configurations: copper male green head white neck ring
Pheasant.texture_assets: Six classes: contour feather, long tail/flight feather, eye, bill/claw keratin, scaled foot skin and bare facial skin. Shared feather detail with separate male copper/green and female mottled masks; barred tail and wing feather striping follow actual panels.
Pheasant.sex_age_season: Adult male display plumage and red face patch must remain linked. Females/juveniles use cryptic brown patterns rather than merely dimming the male. Plan tail length and facial ornament with sex/age; no universal male-bright rule for other birds.
Pheasant.extras: Male red eye skin and small ear tufts, sex-appropriate tail proportions and subtle leg-spur option after approval. Do not glue female coat onto an excessively long male tail without a shape review.
Pheasant.paint_details: Bare red facial region stays outside the glossy eyeball and integrates with feather edges. Neck ring is feather pigmentation, not a mesh/material seam. Tail bars line up along feather lengths and remain legible from rear.
Pheasant.hypotheses: Reduced ring contrast and darker forest body are optional patterns. Golden-pheasant style cape/crest is not treated as a simple palette of a ring-necked body.
Pheasant.geometry_limits: Current generic bird motion does not prove a realistic pheasant burst takeoff or ground run. Strongly different pheasant taxa and male/female tail extremes may need additional selected shapes.

real_analogues: Small minnow-like body plans
Fathead-minnow breeding male as one colour-state reference, not a global species template
Small native freshwater fish (guild).texture_assets: Three classes: small-scale body detail, translucent fin/membrane with rays and eye/cornea. Share one scale and one fin source. Dorsal/ventral, lateral stripe, tail-base spot and breeding-head masks produce variants; no2K texture per tiny fish.
Small native freshwater fish (guild).sex_age_season: Use species-specific breeding colour states only where supported. A dark breeding head/tiny tubercle normal is appropriate to the fathead analogue, not every fish. Juveniles can share a smaller compatible body after proportion checks; eggs/larvae remain separate representations.
Small native freshwater fish (guild).extras: Small optional barbel or tubercle normal only for a compatible lineage. Keep actual fin count/placement, gill cover and mouth orientation consistent with the selected model; do not invent random fin appendages.
Small native freshwater fish (guild).paint_details: Countershade darker above/paler below with continuous flank scale direction. Lateral stripe and gill cover must follow anatomy. Fin alpha and ray detail should avoid large overdraw; eye gloss is local, not an emissive whole-body silver sheen.
Small native freshwater fish (guild).hypotheses: Subtle amber, darker pool mottling and weaker stripe variants can support invented native lineages. Not every region receives the same Earth minnow species or decorative aquarium colours.
Small native freshwater fish (guild).geometry_limits: Minnows, livebearers, sticklebacks and characins can differ in fin topology/body shape; pick compatible silhouettes or add another model. A fish-source swim transfer is only a raw audition and does not provide school AI or feeding automatically.

real_analogues: Wood mouse
Deer-mouse-like two-tone body/tail
Mouse.texture_assets: Five classes: short body fur, fine tail skin/fur, eye, nose/paw/lid skin and ear skin. Shared neutral fur with dorsal/ventral, tail-top/underside and facial masks. Tail covering is lineage-specific; do not paint all mice with a naked rat tail.
Mouse.sex_age_season: Share the coat pool across sexes; no invented male-only bright ornament. Later juveniles need ear/head/body proportions, while dependent naked pups remain outside the visible adult prototype. Seasonal density changes should not turn ordinary woodland mice winter white.
Mouse.extras: Prominent but fitted lateral eyes/lids, muzzle whiskers and bounded ear/tail traits. Delicate paws and tail remain low detail at normal distance; do not add expensive hair cards to every ambient mouse.
Mouse.paint_details: Soft body fur must meet sparse ear/nose skin smoothly. A deer-mouse analogue has a defined two-tone tail and pale feet/underside; a wood-mouse-like tail has its own covering. Preserve symmetrical nose/eye landmarks even with asymmetrical fur noise.
Mouse.hypotheses: Paler dry substrate and darker cover-associated pigments are bounded art hypotheses. Do not randomize extreme piebald domestic mouse patterns into every wild lineage.
Mouse.geometry_limits: African forest-mouse and Rajah spiny-rat aliases still need their own references; coarse spines, size and skull differences may require another approved shape. This refinement does not claim they are equivalent to a wood mouse.

real_analogues: Eastern grey squirrel including dark morphs
Other tree-squirrel colours as provisional silhouettes, not exact species matches
Squirrel.texture_assets: Six classes: short head/body fur, long tail fur, eye, nose/lid skin, paw skin and claw keratin. Share two fur detail sources; tail-edge frost and dorsal/ventral masks generate colour variants without another atlas per tint.
Squirrel.sex_age_season: Same basic coat choices for both sexes, with only modest overlapping size/proportion changes later. Tail fullness and seasonal coat density are linked style states; not a mandatory universal colour swap. Young require proportion checks before simple scaling.
Squirrel.extras: Bounded tail length/fullness, occasional lineage-specific ear tufts, muzzle whiskers and fitted lids after approval. Keep the tail animated through its actual hierarchy rather than an independent rigid fluffy prop.
Squirrel.paint_details: Long fibres follow the tail curve, with fine grizzle rather than a painted solid stripe. Belly and muzzle transitions stay broad and fur-soft. Dark morphs retain enough fibre/roughness variation to read in shade.
Squirrel.hypotheses: A muted brown or altered tail frosting is an optional woodland lineage design. Melanism is a pigment variant, not evidence of another body species.
Squirrel.geometry_limits: Flying-squirrel membranes, giant-squirrel proportions, chipmunk stripes/body and ground-squirrel posture are not automatically supported by a generic tree-squirrel mesh. Ground squirrel is already a separate roster entry.

real_analogues: Przewalski's horse, the roster's named horse analogue
Horse.texture_assets: Six classes: short body fur, coarse mane/tail hair, eye, muzzle/lid skin, hoof keratin and ear skin. Shared fur and mane sources; dorsal stripe, dark points, pale underside/muzzle and optional subtle leg bars are mask controls.
Horse.sex_age_season: Baseline sexes share dun coat; plan overlapping size/neck fullness after motion approval. Winter density is not a domestic grey/white coat gene. Foals require leg/body/head proportions and mane development later, not simply shrinking an adult.
Horse.extras: Upright dark mane with no long domestic forelock, dark tail hair, fitted eyes/lids and muzzle whiskers. Optional bounded mane density is allowed only after checking the selected silhouette.
Horse.paint_details: Keep the dorsal line continuous into the mane/tail, darken lower legs and preserve pale ventral/muzzle regions. Fine body hair should not look like deer spots. Hoof rim and muzzle nostrils need deliberate anatomical masks.
Horse.hypotheses: A darker primitive-horse analogue or modest primitive-marking variation can be invented. Bay/chestnut/black/grey domestic palettes are optional separate lineages, not presented as normal Przewalski coat variation.
Horse.geometry_limits: The named analogue is stocky with a substantial head/neck and short legs. A generic slender riding-horse mesh cannot become exact Przewalski anatomy through dun paint alone; inspect the silhouette and choose another candidate if needed.

real_analogues: Caribou/reindeer adult sexes and seasonal coat
Reindeer.texture_assets: Five classes: dense fur, eye, nose/lid skin, hoof keratin and antler bone/velvet. Reuse the deer fur source at a coarser scale. Neck/rump/flank/feet masks and winter whitening are linked configurations; antler material is separate from coat.
Reindeer.sex_age_season: Both sexes may carry antlers; sex-specific rack size and seasonal shedding must replace the ordinary-deer horn/no-horn shortcut. Larger mature bulls have heavier racks, cows generally more slender ones. Calves need their own age coat/proportions; no generic spotted-fawn rule.
Reindeer.extras: Three compatible rack profiles with sex/age size ranges, seasonal bare/velvet/no-rack states, broad hoof silhouette and modest neck fringe. These are planned extras only, not generated or installed yet.
Reindeer.paint_details: Pale neck, rump, lower legs and possible flank stripe need anatomical placement. Fur length changes gradually at neck/shoulders; dark nose/lids and hooves remain outside whitening masks.
Reindeer.hypotheses: Paler tundra and darker wooded forms are bounded lineage palettes. Do not force annual all-white coat or random antler presence independent of age/sex/season.
Reindeer.geometry_limits: Broad hooves, muzzle and neck proportions distinguish the selected body from a generic doe. Large tundra-versus-woodland silhouette changes need a second shape or explicit approved morph.

real_analogues: Moose adult male/female and unspotted calf
Moose.texture_assets: Six classes: coarse body fur, longer bell/neck fur, eye, nose/lid skin, hoof keratin and antler bone/velvet. Shared deer coarse-fur source; face, leg and bell masks and a calf palette do most of the work. Antler palm normal shares bone detail, not fur.
Moose.sex_age_season: Mature males carry seasonal antlers; females lack the normal rack. Both sexes can have a throat bell, with linked size/proportion variation rather than treating it as a male-only accessory. Calves are reddish-brown without the ordinary-deer white fawn spots.
Moose.extras: Three palmate rack outlines plus juvenile narrower racks and seasonal none/velvet states. Keep a drooping muzzle, long legs and bell attached to the proper head/neck bones; no deer-head recolour shortcut.
Moose.paint_details: Coarse fibres blend continuously through shoulder and neck. Muzzle/lid skin placement is especially important on the large face. Calf rust colour is an age state; lower legs and antlers retain their own material masks.
Moose.hypotheses: Subdued lighter upland or darker wet-woodland pigment can be proposed; these are not new verified moose species. Avoid high-contrast adult spots as the default.
Moose.geometry_limits: Generic deer proportions cannot be patched into moose by antlers alone. Bell and heavy muzzle must survive feeding/head turns; large rack variants need clearance checks after owner selection.

real_analogues: Banteng as a sourced wild-Bos colour/sex analogue
Other wild-cattle silhouettes remain separate review decisions
Wild cattle.texture_assets: Five classes: short coat, eye, muzzle/lid skin, horn/hoof keratin and ear skin. One fur source; rump/stocking/muzzle/eye-patch masks for the banteng analogue, plus optional dorsal stripe for an explicitly invented lineage.
Wild cattle.sex_age_season: Both sexes have horns, with size/curvature and heavier male forequarters linked to maturity. For the banteng analogue, mature males are darker and females/young more rufous. Do not apply that rule indiscriminately to all wild cattle or interpret every dark coat as male.
Wild cattle.extras: Two horn-direction families with male/female/young sizes, modest dewlap and tail tuft after approval. Match horns to the selected skull and do not retain an adult heavy bull chest on a purported calf.
Wild cattle.paint_details: White lower legs, rump, muzzle ring and small eye-region marks are separate anatomical masks in the banteng analogue. Blend short fur through neck/chest; bare muzzle and horn bases need local roughness, not bright painted highlights.
Wild cattle.hypotheses: A subdued darker dorsal-stripe open-woodland lineage is an optional art design. Do not claim a recreated aurochs from a generic black coat without dedicated anatomical/reference work.
Wild cattle.geometry_limits: Banteng, gaur and extinct aurochs differ beyond paint; select compatible candidate bodies or later approve another archetype. This planning does not add named species to the simulation.

real_analogues: Ruffed-grouse grey/red-brown morphs
Grouse.texture_assets: Five classes: contour feather, flight/tail feather, eye, bill/claw keratin and foot skin. Share two feather sources; body mottling, neck ruff and terminal tail band are masks, with palette changes over the same detail.
Grouse.sex_age_season: Ruffed-grouse-like sexes share cryptic plumage; no obligatory bright male. Display ruff/tail proportions are linked later traits. Chicks need a juvenile/down shape; winter density does not imply ptarmigan whitening.
Grouse.extras: Small crest, optional ruff and coherent tail fan after approval. Fan/drumming display remains a missing animation until supplied.
Grouse.paint_details: Fine bars and pale feather spots over a warm/grey base, with the broad dark near-terminal tail band placed deliberately. No mammal-fur collar seam.
Grouse.hypotheses: Dark wet-forest and pale woodland palettes or reduced pattern contrast are optional art hypotheses.
Grouse.geometry_limits: Sage-grouse sacs, prairie-chicken ornaments and ptarmigan feet are not generic grouse recolours. Bird Walk/Flap does not supply a drumming action.

real_analogues: Northern bobwhite head-pattern sex pair
Quail.texture_assets: Five classes: contour feather, flight/tail feather, eye, bill/claw keratin and foot skin. Share small feather detail; sex-specific face/throat masks and mottled body maps do not require separate source generations.
Quail.sex_age_season: Bobwhite-like male white brow/throat and female buff brow/throat are linked masks, not a universal quail rule. Juveniles stay cryptic with age-specific proportions.
Quail.extras: Optional short crest or plume only on an approved compatible lineage; compact groundbird body and short tail first. Fit eyes, bill nostrils and toes.
Quail.paint_details: Face stripes follow brow/throat around the eyes. Subtle feather shafts and mottles break up the back; underside transition remains soft.
Quail.hypotheses: Sandy, dark or altered facial-band lineages are optional designs, not asserted bobwhite subspecies.
Quail.geometry_limits: California-quail plumes and coturnix proportions may need other shapes. Burst takeoff and running require motion review rather than a renamed generic clip.

real_analogues: Wild turkey adult sexes and young
Turkey.texture_assets: Six classes: contour feather, tail/flight feather, eye, bill/claw keratin, foot skin and bare head skin. Two feather sources with bar/tip/sheen masks; head skin and beard get separate placement.
Turkey.sex_age_season: Adult males generally larger with stronger head ornaments and beard; some females also have beards. Head colour can be a display state, not a genetic coat. Poults need juvenile/down proportions.
Turkey.extras: Snood, wattles/caruncles, modest beard and tail fan after approval. A natural strut/display is still missing from a generic bird bank.
Turkey.paint_details: Separate bare-skin folds from feathers; wing bars/tail tips follow feather directions. Bronze is restrained sheen, not metallic plastic or emission.
Turkey.hypotheses: Reduced iridescence and altered pale edging are optional; white domestic turkey is not the default wild form.
Turkey.geometry_limits: Heavy domestic or ocellated-turkey forms need separate silhouette/ornament decisions. Sex-specific tail/head extremes must survive motion.

real_analogues: Red junglefowl adult male/female
Junglefowl.texture_assets: Six classes: contour feather, hackle/tail/flight feather, eye, bill/claw keratin, foot skin and comb/face skin. Shared detail with linked sex masks for neck, saddle, breast, face and curved tail.
Junglefowl.sex_age_season: Male hackles, larger comb/wattles and long tail are linked. Females use brown plumage and smaller ornaments. Juveniles must not keep an adult rooster crest/tail; feather wear is separate from sex.
Junglefowl.extras: Two or three comb/wattle sizes, male tail sickles and optional spur after approval. No default ornamental domestic crest or feathered legs.
Junglefowl.paint_details: Golden neck grades by feather rows into the darker body. Bare face/comb use skin maps; eyelid transition stays visible without mammal-style lashes.
Junglefowl.hypotheses: Dark forest and muted rufous patterns are optional. Domestic patchwork and exaggerated ornaments require an explicit alternate lineage.
Junglefowl.geometry_limits: Rooster/hen tail and comb differences require geometry, not colour alone. Generic Walk/Flap does not provide crowing or scratch-forage actions.

real_analogues: Raccoon grey coat, face mask and ringed tail
Raccoon.texture_assets: Six classes: body fur, longer tail fur, eye, nose/lid skin, paw skin and claw keratin. Shared fur with face-mask, pale border, underside and continuous tail-ring masks.
Raccoon.sex_age_season: Coats shared across sexes; modest overlapping size changes only later. Young need shorter muzzle/rounder head proportions. Winter fullness is not a separate inherited species coat.
Raccoon.extras: Fitted eyes/lids, whiskers, rounded furred ears and tactile paws after approval. Tail fullness is bounded and follows the actual chain.
Raccoon.paint_details: Mask follows the eye/cheek anatomy with pale borders, avoiding eyeball-shaped black stickers. Rings wrap continuously around the tail, not square atlas patches.
Raccoon.hypotheses: Subdued dark or pale pigment families are optional; flamboyant masks are not an ecological requirement.
Raccoon.geometry_limits: Ringtail, coati and raccoon dog are not interchangeable raccoon palettes. Paw weights must pass close interaction poses before claiming dexterous hands.

real_analogues: European badger baseline
Badger.texture_assets: Six classes: coarse body fur, short face fur, eye, nose/lid skin, paw skin and claw keratin. Shared fur with facial-stripe, pale ear-edge, dark-leg and dorsal-grizzle masks.
Badger.sex_age_season: Male/female European badgers do not need different face colours. Size distributions overlap. Cubs need juvenile proportions; visible older young develop the familiar pattern rather than staying pink adults.
Badger.extras: Short rounded pale-rimmed ears, fitted lids, whiskers and robust claws after approval. Keep stocky torso and short tail; no sex ornament needed.
Badger.paint_details: Eye stripes run over cheek/forehead with a pale central face. Coarse body fur grades into shorter facial fur without a hard neck seam.
Badger.hypotheses: Warmer/weaker stripes or dark-backed forms are optional lineages, not a universal camouflage prescription.
Badger.geometry_limits: American, honey and hog badgers differ in anatomy; a Meles-like body is not proof it covers them. Crouched poses still need limb/body clearance checks.

real_analogues: American beaver
Beaver.texture_assets: Six classes: dense fur, scaled tail skin, eye, nose/lid/paw skin, claw keratin and incisor enamel. Shared fur tinted modestly; tail, muzzle and webbed rear feet use separate masks.
Beaver.sex_age_season: Coats shared across sexes, no invented male ornament. Wet/dry darkening is a state, not a new species. Kits need age proportions; tail size stays linked to body size.
Beaver.extras: Flat paddle tail and webbed rear feet must be credible in selected geometry. Add paired incisors only where the mouth opens, then whiskers and fitted eyes.
Beaver.paint_details: Tail scales and sparse foot skin stay outside fur masks. Dry/wet roughness differs without turning the animal into glossy rubber; inspect tail-root blend from rear.
Beaver.hypotheses: Paler or rufous pigments are optional. A round rat tail is not a beaver variant.
Beaver.geometry_limits: Rodent gait does not supply swimming, tail slap, felling or wood carrying. The source is a terrestrial audition; missing behaviours remain explicit.

real_analogues: North American river-otter-like fur/head treatment
Otter.texture_assets: Five classes: dense short fur, eye, nose/lid/paw skin, claw keratin and ear skin. Shared fur with throat/muzzle/underside masks. Wet darkening/roughness is a state, not another generated colour map.
Otter.sex_age_season: No sex-coded coat pool; later size ranges overlap. Young need rounded-head/body proportion checks. Wet/dry states preserve lineage patterns; winter density does not force a new colour family.
Otter.extras: Sensitive-looking whiskers, small ears, fitted eyes/lids and tapering muscular tail after approval. Webbed feet need geometry rather than painted gaps between detached toes.
Otter.paint_details: Short fur grades softly into throat. Distinguish bare nose/lids from wet coat with local gloss; avoid a uniform plastic shine.
Otter.hypotheses: Broader pale throat and grey-brown pigment are optional designs, not invented conspicuous sex-only spots.
Otter.geometry_limits: River, giant, clawless and sea otters differ beyond paint. Terrestrial fox-like motion does not supply aquatic propulsion or floating/rest poses.

real_analogues: Canada lynx structure
Eurasian-lynx pattern needs a separate shape check
Lynx.texture_assets: Six classes: body fur, cheek/tuft fur, eye, nose/lid skin, paw pads and claw keratin. Shared fur; spots, cheek ruff, eye surrounds and black tail tip are masks.
Lynx.sex_age_season: Sexes share palettes/patterns; size is a later overlapping proportion trait. Winter coat and furry paws are linked cold-climate traits. Kittens need age proportions, not only extra spots or uniform scale.
Lynx.extras: Short black-tipped tail, ear tufts and cheek ruff after approval. Attach detail to correct head/neck bones; no random sex ornament.
Lynx.paint_details: Spots break into fur along flanks/limbs. Ear tufts/tail tip need correct placement; muzzle/lid skin stays distinct while cheek fur direction remains coherent.
Lynx.hypotheses: Reduced spotting and darker wooded forms are optional; a spotted coat alone does not identify an exact real lynx species.
Lynx.geometry_limits: Canada-like long legs/broad furry paws and Eurasian proportions may need separate shapes. Feline transfer does not prove natural jumping, crouching or hunting.

real_analogues: Tufted round-disc baseline
Barn-owl heart disc is an alternate shape limit
coat_configurations: buff/white heart-disc only on compatible shape
Owl.texture_assets: Five classes: face/body contour feather, flight/tail feather, eye, bill/claw keratin and foot skin. Shared feather sources; disc edge, brow, throat, bars and underside are masks. Iris colour follows the chosen analogue.
Owl.sex_age_season: No universal bright-male coat. Sex-linked size/spotting requires a lineage reference; female-larger is possible rather than a rule for every bird. Owlets need down/age shapes without automatic adult tufts.
Owl.extras: Deliberate facial-disc/brow geometry and compatible tuft/no-tuft states. Seat eyes within a lid/feather socket, not mammal fur. Tufts are feathers, not ears or horns.
Owl.paint_details: Face feathers radiate along the actual disc; breast/wing bars follow feathers. Large eyes are glossy within a feather rim. Pale plumage must still shade correctly at night.
Owl.hypotheses: Darker wet-forest or paler open-habitat patterns are optional; any white owl is not automatically a snowy owl.
Owl.geometry_limits: Barn-owl heart disc/dark eyes/no tufts cannot come from painting a great-horned face white. Owl3 Flap has a recorded distortion warning; valid arrays do not clear it.

real_analogues: Common raven heavy bill, shaggy throat and wedge tail
Raven.texture_assets: Five classes: body feather, flight/tail feather, eye, bill/claw keratin and foot skin. Share feather detail; mantle, coverts, throat and tail masks adjust roughness/tint without another generation per black shade.
Raven.sex_age_season: Adult sexes share black plumage. Brownness/wear is age-linked; later size differences retain overlapping ranges and functional wings.
Raven.extras: Heavy arched bill, minimal nasal bristles, throat hackles and wedge tail after shape approval. Avoid excessive overlapping feather cards.
Raven.paint_details: Black feathers need restrained fibre/roughness and directional sheen to read in shade; bill/eye gloss stays local. A tail wedge is geometry, not a triangular painted patch.
Raven.hypotheses: Subdued grey-black or shifted sheen is optional. Bright piebald adults are not the baseline common raven.
Raven.geometry_limits: Crow/rook/chough heads and tails are not guaranteed raven recolours. Generic bird clips do not supply bill manipulation, social gestures or every hop. Existing audio is separate until integration.
